steps.body: **Association** is the overall direction of the dots. **Positive**: as x goes up, y tends to go up (dots rise to the right). **Negative**: as x goes up, y tends to go down (dots fall). **No association**: no clear direction.

widget.prompt: On a scatter plot, the dots rise from the lower-left to the upper-right. What association is this?

options.label: Positive
options.feedback: Right — rising-to-the-right dots show a positive association.

options.label: Negative
options.feedback: Negative dots FALL to the right — these RISE, so it's positive.

options.label: No association
options.feedback: There's a clear upward direction, so it's a positive association, not none.

options.label: Can't tell
options.feedback: The dots clearly rise to the right — that's a positive association.

predict.prompt: Can a scatter plot show a real association even when the dots DON'T form a perfect line?

options.label: Yes — a loose band still tells a story
No — association needs a perfect line
Only with at least ten dots

predict.reveal: Association is about the overall drift, not perfection — dots can scatter around a trend and still rise together convincingly.

steps.body: Think about what the pairing means. More hours of studying and more problems solved rise together — positive. More time driving and less fuel left in the tank move oppositely — negative. Shoe size and test score have no real link — no association.

explanationVariants: Dots falling from upper-left to lower-right show a negative association: as x rises, y drops.
Falling-to-the-right dots are a negative association.

widget.prompt: The dots fall from the upper-left to the lower-right. What association is this?

options.label: Negative
options.feedback: Right — falling-to-the-right dots show a negative association.

options.label: Positive
options.feedback: Positive dots RISE to the right — these FALL, so it's negative.

options.label: No association
options.feedback: There's a clear downward direction, so it's negative, not none.

options.label: Zero
options.feedback: 'Zero' isn't a direction here — falling dots are a negative association.

widget.prompt: As a candle burns longer, its height gets smaller. What association do burn-time and height have?

options.label: Negative
options.feedback: Right — more burn-time means less height, so they move oppositely: negative.

options.label: Positive
options.feedback: They move OPPOSITELY (more time, less height), which is a NEGATIVE association.

options.label: No association
options.feedback: There's a clear link — more time, less height — so it's a negative association.

options.label: Both positive and negative
options.feedback: It's consistently opposite: more time, less height — a negative association.

explanationVariants: Scattered dots with no upward or downward drift show no association between the measurements.
No clear direction means no association.

widget.prompt: A scatter plot of students' shoe sizes vs. their math scores shows dots scattered with no clear direction. What association is this?

options.label: No association
options.feedback: Right — no upward or downward pattern means no association.

options.label: Positive

options.label: Negative

options.label: Strong
options.feedback: With no direction at all, there's no association — weak or strong doesn't apply.

explanationVariants: More practice hours tends to mean more baskets made — they rise together: positive.
Both increase together, so it's a positive association.

widget.prompt: The more hours players practice free throws, the more baskets they tend to make. What association is this?

options.label: No association

items.label: hours studied & test score

hints: Ask: as one goes up, does the other go up, go down, or not respond?
Up-together = positive. One up, other down = negative. No link = none.
Positive: studying/score, distance/calories. Negative: car-age/value, temp/cocoa. None: height/vocabulary.

steps.body: Association is the overall direction: positive rises, negative falls, none has no pattern.
takeaways: Positive: dots rise to the right (x up, y up).
Negative: dots fall to the right (x up, y down).
No association: no clear upward or downward direction.
